dossiers.dated_milestone: 2026-11-27 FDA PDUFA target action date, BBP-418 NDA for LGMD2I/R9. Priority Review, no advisory committee planned. Reconfirmed in the Q3-2026 release dated 2026-10-29.
dossiers.kill_risk: The event is real but only a small part of BridgeBio's value, and most of the approval looks priced in. BBP-418 is filed on a 12-month interim read of a surrogate marker (glycosylated alphaDG) plus motor and lung data. A CRL, a delay, or a narrow accelerated-approval label (for example a demand for confirmatory 36-month FORTIFY data; EU regulators have reportedly already asked for 36-month data, pushing the EU filing to 1H-2028) would take roughly $8-10 a share off. Approval adds only about $4, because Attruby revenue ($253M in Q3) drives the stock and the shares already ran from $66.8 to $79.2 into the date. The setup is sell-the-news shaped: the payoff is asymmetric the wrong way even at a high approval probability.
dossiers.thesis_summary: The FDA decision on BBP-418 (LGMD2I/R9, the first potential therapy for the disease) is dated 2026-11-27, 17 days out. It is binding, has not fired, and resolves on its own facts. The basis: Phase 3 FORTIFY met all primary and secondary endpoints at the 12-month interim, the review is Priority, no AdCom is planned, and October data showed cardiac and disease-marker normalization. The company has said it is launch-ready, with more than 600 genetically confirmed patients identified and the US field force deployed. The downside is cushioned by a commercial franchise: Attruby US net revenue was $253.2M in Q3-26 and cash is $1.5B. The other side of that cushion is that BBP-418 is a minority value driver in a $15.4B market cap, so the approval leg is small.

fair_value_target: board null -> 83 (win leg). Arithmetic: ~194.8M shares ($15.43B / $79.2). BBP-418 risk-free NPV is about $3.3B, roughly $17/share, assuming ~$0.6-0.8B peak in an ultra-rare indication. The market already prices about 85% of it, so approval adds about 15% x $17 = ~$2.5, plus a ~$1.3 de-risking re-rate: 79.2 + 3.8 = ~83.

downside_floor: board null -> 70 (lose leg). A CRL more likely means delay or resubmission than an outright kill, so it takes about 50-60% of the $17/share BBP-418 value, or ~$9: 79.2 - 9.2 = ~70. The Attruby franchise and $1.5B cash keep the stock well above the June max-fear print (~62-67), which is likely stale-low for the floor.

win_prob: board null -> 0.88. Priority NDA, every endpoint met, no AdCom, and the company says it is launch-ready; capped below 0.9 because the approval rests on an interim surrogate (accelerated-approval path).
Cash: skeptic's figure of $940.2M (3/31/26) -> $1.5B at 9/30/26 per the Q3 release. Attruby: $180.6M Q1 -> $253.2M Q3.
dossiers.dossier_note:
Live record (FMP quote and press releases, plus web search, 2026-11-10). The PDUFA date is still 2026-11-27, reconfirmed in the Q3-26 release of 10-29. No CRL, extension, or AdCom has been announced, and the catalyst has not fired. Days to milestone: 17.

Binary R:R at $79.2:
- Win leg 83: +3.8, about +4.8%.
- Lose leg 70: -9.2, about -11.6%.
- Payoff ratio about 0.41.
- EV = 0.88 x 3.8 - 0.12 x 9.2 = +2.2/share, about +2.8%.
- Breakeven win probability is about 71%.
The asymmetry is unfavorable because BBP-418 is an ultra-rare asset (LGMD2I, ~7k US+EU patients) inside a $15.4B company whose value is driven by Attruby. Idiosyncrasy holds, but the dated event explains only a fraction of the share price.

TAKEOUT LENS (bio):
- BBIO is a commercial-stage, multi-asset company with three near-term PDUFAs. Beyond BBP-418, infigratinib for achondroplasia has a PDUFA of 2027-02-04 (Priority Review), and encaleret for ADH1 is filed. That makes it strategically scarce for large-cap cardio-renal or rare-disease buyers; Novartis and Amgen are illustrative.
- No named comparable deal was verified in this pass, so the win leg is NOT lifted for takeout. It is undated optionality only.
- The regime caveat applies: XBI at a 5-year high means the ~85-88% approval probability is already rich in the price.

Other notes:
- Board live_price 66.8 dates from June.
- The October 5 BBP-418 cardiac-marker release (HS troponin normalization) strengthens the label case.
- The EU path has slipped, reportedly to a 36-month-data filing in 1H-2028. That is irrelevant to the US date but signals regulator appetite for longer data.

Sources: FMP quote and press releases (BBIO, 2026-11-10); GlobeNewswire Q3-26 release (2026-10-29); musculardystrophynews.com 'FDA to decide on potential first therapy for LGMD2i by late November'; biospace.com acceptance release (2026-05-27).

cro.live_edge_check: Live price $79.22 (FMP quote 2026-11-10; IBKR last 79.23, bid/ask 79.19/79.27). This is the same price the dossier used ($79.2), so the edge has not shrunk since the dossier. Against the dossier legs (win 83, lose 70): upside +3.78 (+4.8%), downside -9.22 (-11.6%), payoff ratio 0.41, EV = 0.88 x 3.78 - 0.12 x 9.22 = +2.22/share (+2.8%), breakeven win probability about 71%. The edge is positive only through the 0.88 probability, and the payoff is the wrong way round (risk $2.4 to make $1). One CRL wipes out about 2.4 approvals' worth of gain. At ~$76.5 the R:R is about 1:1 (+6.5/-6.5) and EV is about +4.9/share (+6.4%), and today's low was $76.60, so that level is reachable. Entering at $79.2 means a thin, probability-dependent edge. A limit closer to 1:1 keeps the edge clearly positive even if the approval probability is a little rich.

cro.tradeability_note: Equity is easy to trade: 90-day average dollar volume is about $214M a day, the quoted spread is 1 bp (79.19/79.27), and no short leg or borrow is needed. Options are NOT acceptable. In the Jan-15-2027 chain, the 80 call is 3.80/7.80 (about 69% wide, OI 152) and the 80 put is 4.30/6.80 (about 45% wide, OI 278). Midpoint IV is about 40-44% against 38% 30-day realized vol. The quoted markets are too wide to express a binary of +4.8%/-11.6%.
cro.window_note: PDUFA is 2026-11-27 (Priority Review, no AdCom planned), 17 days out, reconfirmed in the Q3 release of 2026-10-29. It has not slipped: no major-amendment extension was found, and the single aggregator 'extended' label is unbacked. The instrument is equity, so expiry does not matter. For reference, the first monthly past the date with margin would be Jan-15-2027 (Dec-18 is only 3 weeks after). That expiry exists but is untradeable on spread. The risk to the window is an FDA extension of the action date (+3 months), not timing against an expiry.

director.memo: Promotion run, no seat added; the held book is unchanged: AGIO, SVRA and ANNX, each at 16.67% of NAV, all in FDA/biotech. The only survivor was BBIO, my own first-in-line nomination. It fails two separate tests at today's price and window. First, edge: at $79.2 (up 18.6% since the June $66.8 mark) the 83/70 legs give +4.8% / -11.6%, a payoff ratio of 0.41 and an EV of only +2.8%, carried entirely by the 0.88 approval probability. That is sell-the-news shaped and not as good as the median seat already held, so adding it would shrink every held seat to 12.5% for a thinner bet. Second, expression: it is a binary_prob name, so the hard gate allows only defined-risk structures, but the CRO priced the options as untradeable (Jan-27 80C about 69% wide, 80P about 45% wide) and approved equity only. There is no compliant structure. I kept BBIO on the watchlist as de-prioritized, with a concrete re-entry (at or below $76.50 plus a quotable defined-risk spread, filled before 11-25), so the call is scored at the 11-27 PDUFA rather than silently dropped. The other carried names are re-nominated unchanged, with no stance change, because this run supplied no fresh dossiers on them. Operator flag: 'PVLA_PLACEHOLDER_REMOVED' is a placeholder artifact in the on-deck ledger and should be cleaned up by hand. Cluster mix: 100% FDA/biotech across 3 seats (2 approval decisions, 1 clinical readout). This concentration is a judgement call, not a rule breach, and I would welcome driver diversity from the next full run. Regime notes: the M&A/XBI regime block is dated 2026-07 and is stale as of today (2026-11-10), so I ignored it. I did not lift the BBIO win leg for takeout. The DISCIPLINE phase is advisory only. It would actually favour BBP-418, an approval with near-term launch revenue that pays cash soon, so the pass is driven by price and expression, not by the phase.
